chapter_title: Concerning the Garment of the Waters: how great is

spiritual_reading.full_translation:
When the good that engages directly with evil took on the outermost conditions required for combat, and held steady against the first uprising of opposition formed in active falsity, it defied the dominant evils that rule by persuasive force. Their reach was beyond any ordinary measure, surpassing what countless multiplied states can comprehend. At the beginning of the resistance, that good allowed those evils to take into themselves the burning of their own distorted love and the volatility of their persuasive reasoning; and afterward it permitted the evil that tends to spiritual death to take on an outward covering of truth in its lowest degree. The ruling evils drew that truth into themselves and consumed it by turning it into falsity. From that outward truth, once seized and perverted, abundant derivative falsities poured out, and streams of reasoning flowed on; and the receptive craving of those evils, together with the powers that labor to destroy good and truth, strained to bring those outflows forth.

A full process of such streams, like a principal current of truth flowing with intelligence, entered the craving of each ruling evil; yet no influx could be gathered into a single satisfied reception and brought to rest, because as each descent reached their inmost appropriation it tormented them with the fire and heat of their own love. Those evils were self-renewing persuasions of deception; they were not exhausted, and continual descent of obscured and falsified influence sustained them through the whole span of their existing states.

This shows the scale of the conflict, because it has brought into view destructive affections with gigantic force. They remain entangled, held in constraint, and fixed throughout the whole range of their domain. They are kept from open manifestation and are not presented to the perception of everyone who lives in the merely natural degree under the rule of spiritual death, though in their own order they are made manifest. The entire structure of merely natural life separated from what is living will be ended and dissolved, and its appearances will pass away in an instant. Those evils will be destroyed by the outburst of their own furious persuasion, more devastating than any external shock.

What appears as a small outward comprehension is almost nothing beside the immeasurable abundance of falsities that arise from interior things when truth is seized and inverted. For what is known in externals is only one stream out of innumerable streams from inner arcana that are not disclosed to the natural mind.

Turn your attention to this and be astonished at the measure of truth even in its lowest form, and at the burden borne by the Divine Humanity in carrying such an outward covering through conflict. Understand the greatness of the Divine in active power: the scope of what was permitted for the sake of victory exceeded the measure of the good that entered the outermost combat, and thus an immense work was accomplished.

spiritual_reading.overall_coherence: Coherent as a single spiritual movement: combat with ruling evils, their perversion of outward truth into falsity, the endless unsatisfied intake, the constraint and concealment of destructive affections, the final dissolution of merely natural life, and a concluding call to perceive the magnitude of truth’s lowest degree and the Divine work. The main stumble is the source’s abrupt element-to-garment transition and the syntactic knot in the final comparison, but the spiritual narrative remains continuous.

findings.diagnosis: Mostly coherent correspondential substrate, but the paragraph contains a small seam where two different explanatory frames (elements → garment-of-waters) have been stitched together. The spiritual reading explicitly felt an abrupt transition; that is best explained as an editorial bridge/condensation rather than a full administrative insertion.
findings.evidence: Text: “At the time when the First Man assumed the elements… At the start… he gave them fire and wind; and afterwards he gave the garment of the waters…” The chapter title and the paragraph’s latter half are about “the garment of the waters,” but the opening clause is a broader ‘elements’ frame. The spiritual reading notes: “slightly forced in wording because the source shifts abruptly from one set of elements to the garment theme.” That is exactly what a seam looks like in this dossier: a compiler has prefaced a water-garment unit with a more general ‘elements’ recollection, probably to harmonize with adjacent combat-material.

findings.diagnosis: Genuine difficulty due to damaged/compressed wording, not a voice intrusion. The imagery continues the same functional teaching (insatiable intake, burning descent), but the last sentence is fragmentary and ungrammatical, producing the stumble noted in the spiritual reading.
findings.evidence: Text: “Those rulers were like the [images] of [deception]; they were not emptied; rain and [mist] their existent days.” This is not administrative (no jurisdictions, stations, ranked lists), but a broken poetic/physical simile (emptied; rain/mist) that should support the functional point: continual inflow without satiation. The spiritual reading: “odd cadence of the final line suggest a textual compression; the intended sense still reads as continual sustaining influx.” Removing it would not improve narrative flow; it is already the narrative’s continuation but in damaged form.

findings.diagnosis: Clean correspondential unit: it shifts from hydraulic mechanics to visibility/constraint and eschatological disclosure, but the shift is thematically motivated (what is hidden now will be revealed; the system collapses). No sign of administrative overlay.
findings.evidence: Text: “They are hidden, not revealed… These rulers [also shall be] revealed. The entire universe of flesh will be destroyed…” The spiritual reading reports: “reads cleanly as self-consuming fury; no major resistance.” The teaching remains functional: concealment/revelation, dissolution, and self-destructive ‘voice’ as an internal mechanism (“destroyed with their angry voice”).

findings.diagnosis: Clean correspondential exemplum: the named river (Tigris) functions as a measurable instance to scale an otherwise immeasurable ‘waters’ doctrine. The spiritual reading’s ‘generalization’ is interpretive pressure, not textual corruption or administrative insertion.
findings.evidence: Text: “only one river from thousands of rivers of water… is the river Tigris upon the earth.” This is a classic substrate move: concrete natural object → proportion/scale teaching (one visible stream vs innumerable hidden streams). The spiritual reading: “comparison to a specific principal current is absorbed as ‘one stream’… necessarily generalized.” That is not a narrative break; it is a stable analogy.

findings.diagnosis: Correspondential exhortation with a real syntactic knot at the key comparison (“these waters … greater than the stature of the First Man”). The difficulty is best explained as damaged transmission (omitted particles/relative clauses) or conflated exemplars, not an administrative add-on.
findings.evidence: Text: “Marvel at the stature of the Man who bore them. And understand… that god, active in power, the one whom these waters [are greater] than the stature of the First Man…” The spiritual reading: “syntactically difficult… rendered as the permitted scope… exceeding what finite combat-good could bear.” There is no governance/jurisdiction language here; it is doxological conclusion in the same functional register (measure, bearing, stature, greatness). The ‘god… whom these waters are greater than…’ likely lost a comparative connector (e.g., ‘though’ / ‘because’ / ‘so that’), producing the knot.

textual_criticism.summary: 5 findings. No administrative overlay detected; no excision recommended. Two places where the spiritual reading stumbled (¶7 and ¶11) are best diagnosed as damaged/compressed transmission within the correspondential substrate; ¶6 shows a minor editorial seam (elements → garment-of-waters) but not a distinct inserted block.

harmonized_paragraphs.text: [At] the time when the First Man assumed the elements, and stood [fi]rm against the first enmity that had come about in the darkness, he defied these great and powerful rulers. They are immeasurable, greater than the extent or size of thousands and ten thousands of parasangs. At the start, when he spread the fight against them, he gave them fire and wind; and afterwards he gave the garment of the waters to the rulers of death. So they, the rulers, drank in and consumed those waters, [the way that I told] you [about it]. Many [waters] poured forth from the garment of waters [and from them] the rivers flow. The mouth of the rulers [received them] those [is not filled by], the warriors of destruction [and all] laboured and brought them forth.

There were seven (rivers), like the great river Tigris [that you] see, flowing in to the mouth of each one of them, as they shall not [be gathered] to a single stomach, to their fill; because in turn the descent to its stomach shall burn them with its fire and heat. Those rulers were like the [images] of [deception]; they were not emptied; rain and [mist] their existent days.

[This] is how great a struggle, since it has [revealed] these creatures of destruction, the mighty giants. Behold, they are entwined, bound, and [fixed] in every place. They are hidden, not revealed before the eyes of every flesh that exists on the land of death [but they are in their place]. These rulers [also shall be] revealed. The entire universe of flesh will be destroyed and dissolved [in that day]; all pass away [in a moment]. They will be destroyed with their angry voice, which is mightier than the thunder.

Now, as this small stream is reckoned [as nothing] before the vastness of these waters of which I have recounted to you. For only one river from thousands of rivers of water, from the secrets that are not revealed, is the river Tigris upon the earth.

See [at these waters] and be amazed at the measure of the elements of the waters. Marvel at the stature of the Man who bore them. And understand how great is that god, active in power, the one whom these waters [are greater] than the stature of the First Man who [assumed] this garment of such size; and how much was made.

changes_summary: No changes made. All findings (¶6–¶11) carried recommendation “none”; no excisions were warranted, and “annotate” actions were not requested.
